purpose: Define PTGAE spelling, capitalization, punctuation, number, date, unit, heading, and quotation defaults for ordinary technical prose.
spelling: Use contemporary General American spelling unless a quoted source, proper name, standard, API, or target locale requires another form.
Do not normalize spelling inside quotations, code, identifiers, citations, titles, or formal notation.
capitalization: Capitalize official office, organization, product, program, and service names according to their canonical records.
Use sentence case for ordinary headings unless an owning publication surface defines another convention.
Do not capitalize common nouns merely to make them sound institutional.
punctuation: Use punctuation to expose sentence structure, not to create dramatic tone.
Prefer a period when a long dash or semicolon does not encode a useful relation.
Use a colon before a compact definition, list, consequence, or claim-status rendering when it improves parsing.
Avoid repeated exclamation marks and decorative ellipses in technical, scientific, executive, and operational prose.
numbersDatesUnits: Use digits for measurements, versions, counts, dates, times, money, percentages, and identifiers unless an owning publication convention requires words.
Attach units to measured values and name the measurement context when needed.
Use ISO 8601 dates in machine-facing resources and unambiguous month-name dates in ordinary external prose when that surface requires readability.
Include time zone or UTC offset when the time could affect execution or interpretation.
headings: Use headings that name the actual subject, decision, operation, or result.
Avoid generic headings such as Overview, Information, Notes, or Conclusion when a concrete heading is available.
quotations: Preserve source wording and quotation boundaries.
Corrections, translations, and normalizations of quoted text are separate operations with provenance.
